title: 2 men injured in late-night shooting in Dorchester, police say
author: Darin Zullo
bullets: Two men were injured in a late-night shooting in Dorchester, both with non-life-threatening injuries, police said.
The incident occurred around 10:40 p.m. Friday near 31 Hancock St.; one man was hospitalized, the other self-admitted.
Police have not identified the victims or sought any suspects, and the investigation remains ongoing.

title: Woman trapped, injured in second incident on MBTA Davis escalator this year
author: Darin Zullo
bullets: A woman was injured at MBTA Davis Station when her clothing got trapped in an escalator on August 2.
A fellow rider stopped the escalator and assisted the woman, who suffered a hand injury and was hospitalized.
The incident mirrors a previous fatal accident in February, where a man's clothing was trapped in the same escalator.

title: 2 men arrested after allegedly stealing chain, wallet at knifepoint in Dorchester
author: Darin Zullo
bullets: Deivi Yoander Sanchez Aguasvivas, 24, and Luis Miguel Ramirez-Astacio, 26, arrested for armed robbery and assault in Dorchester.
Victim reported robbery at 140 Humboldt Ave. involving suspects on a blue moped armed with a knife.
Aguasvivas pleaded not guilty and is held without bail; Ramirez-Astacio has outstanding warrants, including unarmed robbery charges.

title: It’s not too late to submit your idea for $2 million in Boston spending
author: Morgan Rousseau
bullets: Boston extends participatory budgeting deadline to August 7, allowing more project submissions for $2 million in city funding.
Residents can submit one-time investment ideas reflecting racial and social equity on the city's participatory budgeting website.
Past funded projects include immigrant legal defense fund and rat-resistant dumpsters; voting on final proposals occurs January 15-February 15.

title: Watch: Ceddanne Rafaela hits home runs in back-to-back at-bats
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Ceddanne Rafaela hit home runs in consecutive at-bats for the Boston Red Sox against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Rafaela's first home run was a 389-foot solo shot, giving the Red Sox an early 1-0 lead in the first inning.
His second home run, a 402-foot blast, tied the game 2-2 in the third inning during Saturday's game.

title: Red Sox reportedly attempted to acquire shortstop Elly De La Cruz, turned down by Reds
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: The Red Sox attempted to acquire shortstop Elly De La Cruz from the Reds but were turned down.
Boston's offer for De La Cruz was prospect-based, aiming to fill a pressing shortstop need.
Boston acquired Curtis Mead for infield depth but remains active in seeking a shortstop upgrade.

title: Drake Maye says his shoulder ‘feels great’ as Patriots training camp continues
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Drake Maye reports his throwing shoulder has fully recovered as the Patriots' training camp continues in Foxborough.
Patriots have bolstered their offensive lineup, notably adding wide receiver A.J. Brown in the offseason.
New England starts their 2026-27 season with a Super Bowl rematch against the Seattle Seahawks.

title: If July’s stretch of dominance wasn’t enough, the Red Sox’ win Friday proved they’re plenty capable of a postseason run
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: Boston Red Sox defeated World Series favorites Los Angeles Dodgers 5-4, showing strong postseason potential.
Ceddanne Rafaela played a key role, turning a 4-3 deficit into a 5-4 victory, supported by strong team efforts.
Despite missing key players, Red Sox maintain solid performance and are likely to be active at the trade deadline.

title: Red Sox fend off Dodgers, 9-4, in grindy series opener
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Ceddanne Rafaela hit a go-ahead two-run homer in the seventh, helping the Red Sox defeat the Dodgers 9-4.
Brayan Bello pitched four scoreless relief innings, maintaining a 0.69 ERA in relief and earning the win for the Red Sox.
The Red Sox finished July with a franchise-best 21-4 record, boosting their playoff chances significantly.

title: Gabe Jacas makes his Patriots debut and other takeaways from Day 7 of training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Gabe Jacas, Patriots' 2026 second-round pick, made his practice debut in a limited role on Saturday.
The Patriots' defense recorded two interceptions, showcasing a strong performance in the team's third-straight padded practice.
Undrafted tight end Tanner Arkin is making an impact in camp, earning first-team reps as a blocker.
